subject: Next steps: AP constraints & payment path for Redwood pilot
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Taylor Brooks <taylor.brooks@acmeanalytics.com>, Megan Li <megan.li@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: AP constraints & payment path for Redwood pilot

Hi Taylor / Megan —

Great to meet you both on the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on procurement and get your pilot started without surprises:

What we covered (short):
- Pilot scope: 3-month proof-of-value (up to 1M tokens/month) for two product teams.
- Success criteria: latency under 200ms p95, cost per 1k tokens target <= $0.60.
- Security: SOC2 in progress, we can provide transient log access for evals.

Decision items for AP / procurement team we need to confirm:
1) Payment method: will Acme onboard Redwood as a vendor and issue a PO, or do you prefer to pay by corporate card (one-time or monthly)?
2) Marketplace path: is procurement open to procuring via the CloudMarket (AWS Marketplace) to speed onboarding?
3) Vendor onboarding: we attached a short vendor_onboarding_form.xlsx and a draft pilot SOW for your review. If you need different fields, we can adapt.

Proposed next steps:
- Taylor: confirm whether AP requires a PO threshold (e.g., PO required for >$10k).
- Megan: confirm whether you can use card for an initial trial and whether marketplace procurement is an option.
- We (Redwood): we can generate a short-term card invoice or open a PO-based invoice path — whatever reduces friction.

Attaching:
- vendor_onboarding_form.xlsx (fill and return)
- redwood_pilot_sow_v1.pdf (draft)

If it's helpful, we can schedule a 20-min sync with your procurement contact early next week to walk the options and clarify timelines.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Taylor Brooks <taylor.brooks@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Megan Li <megan.li@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: AP constraints & payment path for Redwood pilot

Thanks Jonas — good summary. A few clarifications from AP side: 

- PO policy: Acme requires a PO for any vendor spend forecasted to exceed $10,000 in a single contract year. For short pilots we sometimes allow a single-month card charge under $3,000, but that requires pre-approval by Finance.
- Vendor onboarding: we need the vendor form completed (that captures W-9 / tax details and banking). Typical onboarding timeline is ~2–3 weeks once the form + W-9 are submitted; if we need legal review for anything non-standard it can add ~1 week.
- Marketplace: Procurement prefers marketplace purchases when available because they simplify billing and approvals. If Redwood is available via our cloud marketplace, procurement can often bypass the vendor onboarding step entirely.

One other constraint: our AP team blocks any vendor without bank account details set up for ACH — paper check is rarely used.

Next steps for us:
- I will check with Finance about the $3,000 card exception for an initial proof-of-value and let you know by EOD Friday.
- If we go PO route, I will need a short SOW with the total not-to-exceed amount and vendor legal name/ID.

Megan — want to add anything on the product side?

Best,
Taylor
Taylor Brooks
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Analytics
(taylor.brooks@acmeanalytics.com)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Taylor Brooks <taylor.brooks@acmeanalytics.com>, Megan Li <megan.li@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 07:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: AP constraints & payment path for Redwood pilot

Thanks Taylor — that helps a lot. Two quick clarifications and an ask from our side: 

1) If Finance can approve a one-month card spend under $3k, we can push a minimal initial test to get product validation while the vendor onboarding runs in parallel. That often shortens time-to-value.
2) If procurement prefers marketplace, we are listed in AWS Marketplace (metered SaaS) — I can share the listing link and provide an estimate SKU we recommend for a 3-month pilot. Using marketplace would mean you get standard terms and immediate provisioning (no vendor form).

Ask: Taylor — would you be able to share the specific PO fields your AP system requires (vendor legal name, remit address, tax ID, contact person)? I attached the vendor_onboarding_form.xlsx as requested; if you prefer we can pre-fill vendor legal name/tax ID in a PO-ready SOW to speed PO issuance.

If helpful, I propose a short three-way call tomorrow at 10am PT (Jonas, Taylor, Megan) to finalize path. Otherwise we can proceed asynchronously — we will:
- prepare two tracks in parallel: (A) marketplace SKU + pricing, (B) PO-ready SOW + vendor details filled.

Let me know which you prefer and I’ll send over the marketplace link and the PO-ready SOW draft.

Thanks —
Jonas

[Attachment: redwood_pilot_sow_v1.pdf, vendor_onboarding_form.xlsx]

From: Megan Li <megan.li@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Taylor Brooks <taylor.brooks@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: AP constraints & payment path for Redwood pilot

On Thu, Jun 11, 2026 at 07:45 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> If helpful, I propose a short three-way call tomorrow at 10am PT (Jonas, Taylor, Megan) to finalize path. Otherwise we can proceed asynchronously — we will:
> - prepare two tracks in parallel: (A) marketplace SKU + pricing, (B) PO-ready SOW + vendor details filled.

This sounds good. Procurement prefer marketplace but timeline is tight for our Q3 kickoff — if you can provide the marketplace SKU and a PO-ready SOW, procurement can decide fastest path.

I can push for the card exception for an initial ~2-week pilot if Finance signs off — I’ll confirm by Friday. In the meantime, please send the marketplace link and the SOW filled with Redwood legal name (Redwood Inference, Inc.), tax ID XX-XXXXXXX, and a not-to-exceed pilot amount ($9,000).

I’ll loop in our Finance ops if needed once we have the PO-ready SOW. Thanks for being flexible on both routes.

— Megan
Megan Li
Product Lead, Conversational AI, Acme Analytics
megan.li@acmeanalytics.com
